_comment: Research pass for 2026-10-05, the first report since 2026-08-21 (the scheduled routine fired weekly but never landed a commit - see README). FRED and every market-data host are still blocked by this environment's egress proxy, so FRED-series values are web-sourced into fred_fallback. SENTIMENT SWEEP WAS PARTIAL: 9 of 19 names were refreshed; the rest carry forward untouched, which is the framework's intended behaviour for a quiet or unsearched name.

spx_current.source: S&P 500 close 2026-10-02, +0.73% (+56.27) on a cooler September jobs report. Essentially flat vs the 7,715.47 close in the 2026-08-21 report.

cape_web.source: gurufocus 41.07 (2026-10-01) and 41.38 (2026-10-02); second-highest in ~150 years behind the 44.2 dot-com peak, and above 40 continuously since May 2026

buffett_indicator.source: gurufocus 235.2% (2026-09-29), the same methodology family as the 237.6% in the last report so the week-over-week is apples-to-apples. buffettindicator.org prints 299.6% ($97.5tn market cap / $32.6tn annualised GDP); both are far past the 200% top-of-range anchor, so the score is 5.0 either way

fiscal.source: CBO FY2026 deficit 5.8% of GDP, unchanged since the last report. Debt/GDP 122.6% is still the Q1-2026 GFDEGDQ188S print - no newer quarterly release sourced, so treat it as a stale denominator

cpi_fallback.source: September 2026 headline CPI +3.6% y/y (Cleveland Fed nowcast, updated 2026-10-02), down from 3.7% in August but UP from the 3.4% used in the last report - inflation re-accelerated over the gap. Core 2.39%

fred_fallback.source: 10y 5.28% and 2y 4.83% on 2026-10-02 (the 10y crossed 5% on 2026-09-14, first time since Oct 2023, and El-Erian flagged 5.22%). HY OAS 3.24% = 324bps on 2026-10-01, up a near-monotonic sequence from 293bps on 09-25: 302, 308, 312, 324. BB 204bps, single-B 329bps, CCC 1,215bps - the widening is across the whole stack

_curve_note: The 2s10s un-inverted on 2024-09-05, still inside the trailing 36 months (it leaves that window in September 2027), so FRAMEWORK 1.7's post-inversion asterisk still applies at +45bps. Note the curve is holding its shape while BOTH ends move up hard - this is a level shift, not a steepening.

fed.stance: HIKED 25bps to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, unanimously - the first increase since 2023 - with the dot plot pointing to one more hike this year (median 4.1% end-2026, no change in 2027, cuts in 2028-29)
fed.read: the headwind became an actual tightening. Warsh: inflation has been 'too high for too long' and the FOMC's confidence standard 'has not been satisfied'. Core PCE has run above 3% every month of 2026

sentiment_updates.name: Yardeni
sentiment_updates.note: DOWNGRADE: the Street-high bull cut his own target. 7,900 is barely above spot, and he lifted his bearish-scenario odds from 20% to 30%

statement.summary: Cut year-end S&P target 8,400 -> 7,900 and said 'proceed with caution' as the 10y passed 5%; forward P/E assumption 19.8 -> 18.6

sentiment_updates.name: Lee
sentiment_updates.note: now the loudest bull on the roster, and openly split from Yardeni: reads the hike as REMOVING the pressure for more, and therefore as yields-down, equities-up

statement.summary: Holds S&P above 8,200 by year-end despite the hike, calls it good news for stocks and predicts a historic Q4 rally

sentiment_updates.name: El-Erian
sentiment_updates.note: CALLED IT: in August he said the Treasury buyback was financial engineering that left long rates untouched. The 10y then went through 5%. His new line - interest-rate risk becoming equity and credit risk - is precisely what the HY tile is now showing

statement.summary: Expects the 10y to stay around 5% even if oil falls, citing a structural bond supply/demand imbalance; 'volatility will be a feature, and elevated yields will be a feature for the rest of the year', and 'the big danger' is rate risk turning into equity and credit risk

sentiment_updates.name: Druckenmiller
sentiment_updates.note: GAP WIDENED, not closed: still positioned long megacap tech from Q2, while publicly arguing rates are too LOW and yield suppression is a subsidy to fiscal procrastination. Bearish bonds, long equities, hawkish Fed - pick two

statement.summary: Says rates are already too low and cuts are unnecessary - 'committee members on the Fed who keep saying Fed fund rates are restrictive are just ridiculous'; WSJ op-ed against Treasury long-bond buybacks: if the 30y must trade at 5.5% 'that isn't a crisis, it is an invoice', and the only durable fix is the primary deficit

sentiment_updates.name: Buffett-Berkshire
sentiment_updates.note: Deployment continued into Q3 under Abel: ~$39.4bn of equities bought across H1, ~$17bn of it Alphabet via the AI-funding secondary, plus a $6.8bn Taylor Morrison homebuilder acquisition closed in July. Full Q3 13F is not due until November. Cash was still $365.5bn at 30 June, so this is deployment, not capitulation - and note he is buying a homebuilder into the exact housing weakness Burry is shorting

statement.summary: Abel's reversal confirmed: 14-quarter net-selling streak broken with ~$20bn net bought, $4.5bn of buybacks against none in 2025

sentiment_updates.name: Dalio
sentiment_updates.note: 24m cut to -4 and conviction to the maximum: he has put a clock on it

statement.summary: Says the US is 'on the brink' and that if the fiscal path does not change a debt shock could hit within two years

sentiment_updates.name: Burry
sentiment_updates.note: THESIS BROADENED from AI/semis to housing and the credit cycle - which is why 36m goes to -3. His mortgage data is the real-economy version of what the HY tile is showing

statement.summary: 'The Big Short is about to repeat itself': rates up six straight weeks, mortgage applications -6% w/w, purchase applications -14% y/y, refis -56% y/y, and serious 90+ day delinquencies up for the first time in five months, +19% y/y. Separately questions how fast Nvidia's AI chips lose economic value, citing the 1968 computer-financing cycle, and calls AI infrastructure commitments liabilities in 'hypergrowth mode'

sentiment_updates.name: Dimon
sentiment_updates.note: No new statement inside the fortnight, but the tape is validating the April letter and his Norges Bank remarks: private-credit default rates hit a record 6.0% (Fitch, April) and HY OAS has widened 54bps since the last report. 'Credit will perform worse than people expect' is becoming measurable rather than rhetorical - the rhetoric>action gap is closing from the data side, not from him

sentiment_updates.name: Marks
sentiment_updates.note: No new memo inside the fortnight, but his private-credit memo is the live thesis: the US private-credit default rate hit a record 6.0% in April (Fitch) and the Proskauer index ran 2.73% in Q1 against 1.84% two quarters earlier - while loan spreads were still tightening. Exactly the 'not being paid for the risk' setup he described

reading_list.title: FOMC statement and Chair Warsh's press conference, 16 September 2026
reading_list.why: The single most important event since the last report: a unanimous 25bp HIKE to 3.75-4.00%, the first since 2023, with one more signalled. My Fed block is no longer a headwind, it is active tightening.

reading_list.title: ICE BofA US High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread (BAMLH0A0HYM2)
reading_list.why: My tripwire, and it is moving: 270bps in August to 324bps on 1 October, widening nearly every session since 25 September. Watch this series, not the index, for the next three weeks.

reading_list.title: Druckenmiller's open letter to Treasury Secretary Bessent on long-bond buybacks
reading_list.why: 'If the 30-year must trade at 5.5%, that isn't a crisis. It is an invoice.' The cleanest statement of why my fiscal tile and my rates tile are the same tile.

reading_list.title: US private credit default rate hits a record 6.0%
reading_list.why: Defaults rising while loan spreads were still tightening is the Marks memo stated as data - and the leading edge of the public HY widening my tripwire just caught.

reading_list.title: Burry: 'The Big Short is about to repeat itself'
reading_list.why: The mortgage data behind his housing turn - refis -56% y/y, serious delinquencies +19% - is the household-side mirror of a 5.28% 10-year, and it is testable week to week.
